Aisha / Jon — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed mutual action plan (MAP) so we can size a dedicated pilot and validate SLOs: 

Top-level SLOs you shared
- Target latency: p95 streaming token latency <= 600ms, p99 end-to-end request <= 1.2s for typical chat flows.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state concurrency ~200 concurrent sessions, peak burst to 400.
- Avg generation length: ~150 tokens; typical prompt size ~70 tokens.
- Mix: ~75% streaming chat (low-latency incremental tokens), ~25% synchronous batch requests.
- Compliance: VPC + HIPAA controls required, data residency in us-east-1.

Proposed validation scope (Redwood):
1) Benchmark comparison: H100 vs A100 80GB across your representative prompt set (we'll use sample prompts you provide).
2) Reserved throughput sizing: target reserved tokens/sec that meets p95 latency under 200 concurrent streaming sessions.
3) Streaming sanity: validate streaming SLOs with small-batch KV cache warmup and prefix caching on representative user journeys.
4) Failure modes: verify graceful fallback to a lower-cost variant under capacity stress.

Deliverables from Redwood (timeline):
- KPI matrix (attached): latency targets, token/sec targets, concurrency curves per GPU profile. (Deliver by 2026-12-06)
- Short GPU comparison brief with cost delta and ops notes (attached).
- Pilot runbook & MAP file for sign-off + proposed kickoff (attached).

Action items / owners
- HelioHealth: share a 50–100-row sample prompt set and 1 week of anonymized traffic profile (Jon/Aisha) — due 2026-12-02.
- Redwood (Marissa): run comparative benchmarks (H100 vs A100) using Helio sample set — deliver results 2026-12-06.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare recommended reserved throughput and pricing sketch for Dedicated — deliver 2026-12-06.
- People sync: pilot kickoff meeting — propose Dec 8, 10am ET (link to follow).

Notes / constraints
- We will do measurements for both streaming and non-streaming RPCs. For streaming we will report token-level p50/p95/p99 and end-to-end first-byte latency.
- For cost modeling we will include quantization/FP16 tradeoffs and estimate per-1M token cost for each GPU profile.

Please confirm the sample prompt delivery timeline and whether Dec 8 works for kickoff. I attached the KPI matrix and a short GPU comparison brief to keep things concrete.

Hi all — quick technical note from the bench planning side so expectations are aligned before we start. Summary of recommended test matrix and a few tradeoffs to be explicit about: 

1) GPU comparison approach- H100 (SXM) 
   - Strengths: lower token p95 for long-context streaming, better memory headroom for larger KV caches (good for chat histories).
   - Tradeoffs: higher hourly cost; better for high SLO/low-tail-latency workloads.

   A100 80GB (ampere)
   - Strengths: cost effective for batch/throughput-heavy jobs; good FP16 throughput for short-medium context.
   - Tradeoffs: slightly higher p99 tails for streaming under bursty concurrency.

2) Quantization and model variants- We'll run each GPU with both FP16 baseline and an INT8/4-bit quantized variant (where model permits) to score latency vs quality. Include Rouge/BLEU-ish token overlap and a rapid human QA sample of ~30 prompts.

3) Reserved throughput sizing heuristic- Given the Helio profile (avg generation 150 tokens, 200 concurrent streaming sessions): our baseline estimate to meet p95 streaming <=600ms is ~1200-1500 tokens/sec reserved on an H100 node profile (final number depends on model family and sequence length distribution). On A100 the same token/sec may push p95 closer to 700-900ms at parity config. We'll quantify in the bench run.

4) Pilot plan & metrics- 2-week pilot: week 1 = smoke + functional streaming correctness + latency sweep; week 2 = sustained load runs for throughput and tail-latency. Metrics we will capture: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end first-byte, CPU/GPU utilization, mem/KV cache hit rate, concurrency vs request-latency curve.

5) Ops and fallback policy- We'll propose an autoscale policy that maintains reserved throughput for steady-state, allows controlled burst capacity, and a graceful downgrade to a quantized model (lower-cost) when utilization > 85% for > 3 minutes.

I'll kick off the bench matrix once Vivek confirms we have the right sample set and Ben shares the procurement cap (so we can constrain cost sims). Attaching a short PDF that summarizes the GPU tradeoffs and a KPI spreadsheet Vivek attached earlier (same filename).

-M
